summary: Joan Halifax is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She studied at H. Sophie Newcomb Memorial College from around 1960 to 1964 and at the University of Miami from around 1970 to 1973.
Joanna Cook works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She completed her studies under advisor James Laidlaw around 2003–2007 and held a post at Christ's College, Cambridge.

Joanna Gottfried Williams was an Indologist and art historian. She studied at Swarthmore College, Radcliffe College, and Harvard University before serving as a professor at the University of California, Berkeley from around 1967 to 2011.

Joanne Punzo Waghorne specializes in religious studies and Indology. She studied at the University of Chicago under Donald Capps and Frank E. Reynolds, later holding posts at UMass Boston, Bowdoin College, UNC Chapel Hill, and Syracuse University.

Joe Bransford Wilson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and the University of Virginia, where he completed his Ph.D. under Jeffrey Hopkins, later teaching at Virginia and UNC Wilmington.

Joe Cribb is a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of London and served as Keeper of Coins and Medals at the British Museum, later joining the Ashmolean Museum.

Joey Hung is a Buddhist studies scholar. She studied at PLK Fong Wong Kam Chuen Primary School, Po Leung Kuk Centenary Li Shiu Chung Memorial College, and the Hong Kong Academy for Performing Arts, and held a post at Dharma Drum Buddhist College.
Jogendra Singh is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara under the instruction of Uma Shankar Vyas.

Jogindra Nath Samaddar was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. Educated at Bangabasi College and Presidency University, Kolkata, he taught at Pramatha-Manmatha College, St. Columba's College, Patna College, and Patna University.

Johan Elverskog specializes in Buddhist, religious, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at Naropa University, UC Berkeley, and Indiana University, later holding posts at UC Santa Barbara, the Inner Mongolia Academy of Social Sciences, and Southern Methodist University.

Johann Andreas Schmeller was a German linguistics scholar. During his career, he held positions at the Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich from circa 1826 to 1852 and at the Bavarian State Library from circa 1829 to 1852.

Johann Bernoulli was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Basel between circa 1757 and 1763, and later served as a member of the Prussian Academy of Sciences from circa 1764 to 1807.
Johann Christoph Adelung was a linguist who studied at the Kloster Berge school around 1746–1752 and at the University of Halle-Wittenberg from around 1752 to 1754.

Johann Gottfried Eichhorn was a scholar of religious studies and history/archaeology. He studied under Christian Gottlob Heyne at the University of Göttingen, later holding professorships at the University of Jena and the University of Göttingen.

Johann Gottfried Ludwig Kosegarten was an Indology and linguistics scholar. After studying at the University of Greifswald from around 1808 to 1812, he held academic posts at the University of Jena and the University of Greifswald.

Johann Wilhelm Andreas Pfaff worked in Indology and related fields. He studied at the University of Tübingen and held academic positions at the Imperial University of Dorpat, the University of Würzburg, and the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg.

Johanna Engelberta van Lohuizen-de Leeuw was an Indologist and archaeologist. She studied at Utrecht University from circa 1937 to 1949 and held positions at the University of Groningen and the University of Amsterdam.

Johanna Narten was a linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. She studied at Saarland University and under Karl Hoffmann at Erlangen-Nuremberg, where she held an academic post from circa 1961 to 1993.

Johannes Beltz is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who completed his doctoral studies from around 1994 to 1999 at the University of Lausanne and École Pratique des Hautes Études under Johannes Bronkhorst and Marie-Louise Reiniche.

Johannes Bronkhorst was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy scholar. He studied at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, Savitribai Phule Pune University under S. D. Joshi, and Leiden University, serving as a professor at the University of Lausanne from 1987 to 2002.
